title: Rare failures
statement:
Only 3% of machines fail. A model that always predicts "no failure" has accuracy 0.97. What's wrong with it?

[_]{a}

choices: Its recall is 0: it never catches a failure
explanations: Accuracy hides that it misses every failure.
0.97 is right; it's just the wrong metric.
It makes no positive predictions, so precision is undefined.

hints: How many failures does it catch?
solution: With rare positives, accuracy is misleading; recall = 0.
